messages:
Ella Kramer: Quick sync — pushing a compact roadmap proposal for the Optimize toolkit into the sprint doc. High level: 1) batching heuristics, 2) prefix/KV caching patterns, 3) quantization recommendation hints, 4) eval-triggered alerting for quality regressions. Link: https://rwd/inference/roadmap/opt-toolkit-draft :eyes:
Matt Li: nice, can you call out clear launch lanes? e.g., pilot, beta, GA. Customers keep asking for predictable acceptance criteria.
Ella Kramer: yes — draft idea below in the doc. Pilot = internal + 2 lighthouse customers, with basic batching and 1 caching strategy + manual quant recs. Beta = broader customer opt-in, automated recs for quantization and caching, eval-alerts v1. GA = full console UI, rollouts, and SLAs.
Sandeep Rao: we should add performance SLOs per lane. Pilot: p95 < 300ms for short prompts, Beta: p95 < 250ms, GA: p95 < 200ms (assuming the dedicated pools). Also add acceptable cost delta bounds vs baseline.
Jordan P.: +1 on SLOs. For eval-triggered alerts: need definitions — what signals? accuracy regression on golden prompts, hallucination spike, token-level latency spikes. Also define thresholds and a way to suppress noisy signals.
Ella Kramer: Agreed. Proposed signals in doc: 1) eval score drop > 3% over rolling 24h, 2) sample-level failure rate > 1% on a critical prompt set, 3) avg token latency increase > 20% for two consecutive hours. Suppression rules: require 2 signals OR triage tag by oncall within 2 hours to avoid false positives.
Matt Li: For quantization recs, can we start with discrete guidance not auto-apply? e.g., recommend 8-bit/4-bit flavor with expected quality impact and cost savings estimate per model-family. Customers asked to be conservative.
Sandeep Rao: yes — recs-only for Pilot. Beta can have opt-in automated trial runs on a small traffic slice with canary fallback. Need guardrails: no auto-apply if eval delta > threshold.
Jordan P.: UX note — the recs should come with a short confidence tier (high/medium/low) and an example prompt where we saw the biggest delta. That helps customers decide.
tools-bot: Reminder: RFC doc created by @EllaKramer at 1745503210. Please add reviewers using /add-reviewer.
Ella Kramer: Action items I propose before we call this ready for sprint planning: 1) finalize acceptance matrix (Matt/Sandeep), 2) wireframe the simple rec UI + confidence tiers (Jordan), 3) implement eval signal plumbing + suppression logic (Sandeep), 4) create pilot onboarding checklist for 2 lighthouse customers (Ella). Target: have PR for the doc and acceptance matrix by EOD Wednesday.
Matt Li: I can own the acceptance matrix. Will include cost delta examples, SLO measurements, and rollout gating logic (canary %, rollback criteria).
Sandeep Rao: I'll start the eval signal spec and a short proto of the suppression logic. Will post a snippet here when ready.
Jordan P.: I'll mock the UI and a small example CLI for rec export. Will link Figma and sample JSON payloads.
Ella Kramer: Great. If no objections, I'll schedule a 30m triage on Thursday to lock the lanes and acceptance criteria. Please add any edge cases to the doc before then (especially long-seq workloads and mobile batched clients). :calendar:
Matt Li: One edge: streaming + batching interactions — need to document how KV caching affects streaming latency. I'll add a section.
Sandeep Rao: Also note: quantization guidance differs by model family; add model matrix to the doc (llamaX, redwood-v1 compat notes).
Jordan P.: Sounds good. Closing note: keep the pilot lightweight — customers hate heavy integration up-front. Aim for a single SDK flag and a server-side toggle for early trials.
Ella Kramer: Perfect. I'll update the draft and ping reviewers. Thanks all. :tada:
